idiom_name: opaque-struct gateway module over a libcurl easy handle or a sqlite3 connection
implementation_notes: C has no classes, so the gateway is a module: a header that declares an opaque handle plus functions named in the domestic vocabulary, and a .c file where the foreign calls live (curl_easy_init/setopt/perform, or sqlite3_open_v2 plus sqlite3_prepare_v2/sqlite3_step). The connection object is a second opaque struct - one CURL* easy handle, or one sqlite3* with prepared statements - created and destroyed by explicit *_open/*_close functions, so the foreign types never appear in the header. Because C has no exceptions, error translation is a hand-written mapping from return codes (CURLcode, SQLITE_* result codes, EAI_* from getaddrinfo) into the module's own error enum, and every failure path has to release the handle it owns.
pitfalls: Ownership is manual: every error path must curl_easy_cleanup the handle and free the buffer; a missed free leaks, and a double free is undefined behaviour.
A libcurl easy handle is not thread-safe and runs one transfer at a time - use one handle per thread or the multi interface instead of sharing a gateway struct across threads.

SQLite prepared statements belong to the connection they were prepared on, and the default build serialises access; sharing a sqlite3* plus its statements across threads without care corrupts the call.
Return codes are easy to ignore: casting a CURLcode to a domestic error only at the outermost layer loses which layer failed (transport, protocol or payload).
